correctness.rationale: The exact k-fold geometric offspring pgf has parameter p_i^(n-i). Conditional qG has Pr(qG<r)<=r and Pr(qG>R)<=1/R, producing uniform log population-to-score error O_P(log n)=o_P(n) by union bound. With b_n exp(b_n)=n the rare-score marked process at (b_n i/n,(n-i)(-log p_i)/n-b_n) converges to Poisson intensity exp(-x-z)dx dz; exponential late-index and upper-score tail bounds make top-two extraction legitimate. A unit-rate PPP in u=exp(-z) has top spacing -log(U)~Exp(1); independently marking x~Exp(1) proves joint independence. A positive normalized top-two score gap identifies the true founder despite geometric family noise, and 0 <= |log(B1/B2)+log(1-P_n)| <= 2log n transfers to minority mass. Independent bounded simulations at n=500,3000,10000 checked plausible joint behavior but do NOT establish the infinite limit; checked exact geometric pgf and proof inequalities analytically.

value.rationale: The founder index and *rate* of aggregate minority extinction are intrinsic, separate observables of a selective sweep. Their nontrivial joint independence law sharply quantifies fixation beyond existing qualitative dominance, with exact stochastic scaling, and is a useful natural distributional invariant rather than a routine restatement of the top Gumbel law.

final_claim: For independent geometric branching families with p_i iid Uniform(0,1), n>=2, J_n the largest living genotype birth index and P_n the largest population share, (J_n log(n)/n, -log(1-P_n)/n) converges jointly to two independent unit-rate exponentials.
limitations: No finite-n exact exponential claim; no almost-sure or uniform rate; independence only asymptotic.
Uniform iid p_i, geometric offspring without extinction and independent families are essential.
